title: Possible {name} in source
description: A string shaped like {name} was found in source. The token is a permanent, store-bound Admin API credential: anyone with repository access can call the Shopify Admin API until the app is uninstalled or the token is rotated. Shape-only: this does not prove the credential is live.
remediation: Rotate or recreate the token in the Shopify admin (Apps > API credentials) or uninstall the app to revoke it, audit Admin API access logs for the exposed value, and load the replacement from a secret manager at run time.
limitation: Prefix evidence: Shopify's own developer documentation shows adminApiAccessToken set to an shpat_ value (https://shopify.dev/docs/api/shopify-app-remix/latest/guide-custom-apps, retrieved 2026-10-16). Body charset/length is NOT specified in Shopify's official documentation: the pattern lower-bounds the body at 32 alphanumeric characters (covering the observed 32-hex and 32-64-alphanumeric family shapes) and leaves the upper bound open so longer tokens are not missed. Bodies outside [A-Za-z0-9] or shorter than 32 characters would be missed. Shopify's shpss_ (app client secret) and shpca_ (custom-app access token) are different token types and are deliberately not matched.
fp: Documentation examples using the shpat_ prefix with placeholder bodies (for example shpat_1234567890) are the common false positives; the 32-character body floor and the placeholder denylist veto them.
recordDesc: {name} values start with the fixed prefix shpat_ followed by a random body run. A committed value grants Admin API access to the store the app is installed on within its granted scopes, so exposure is high-impact even though the match alone cannot prove the token is active.
applicability: Any source, configuration, or CI file that embeds a Shopify custom-app or OAuth Admin API access token.
risk: A committed Admin API token exposes store data and write operations (orders, products, customers) within the app's granted scopes until it is revoked.
why: A leaked {name} keeps working until the app is uninstalled or the token is rotated, so committed copies are high-impact even in old commits.
fix: Revoke the exposed token (uninstall the app or regenerate credentials in the Shopify admin).
Audit Admin API access logs for use of the exposed value.
Store the replacement outside version control (environment variable or secret manager) and rotate on any suspected exposure.
verifyT: After rotation, confirm the old value no longer authenticates (a request with it returns 401) and that a fresh secret scan of the repository reports no shpat_ shape.
